name: go-dangling-cross-file-referrer-asks
desc: removing a def that ANOTHER file still references (per the refs index) is the real 'you'll break callers' signal → ask

name: go-dangling-self-only-referrer-clean
desc: removing a def whose ONLY referrer is the edited file itself is legitimate — self-exclusion drops the sole referrer → no ask. enrolled_refs pins that the referrer WAS enrolled, so the silence is self-exclusion, not an empty index

name: go-dangling-def-redefined-in-the-same-edit-clean
desc: the definition is removed and RE-ADDED in the same edit — a signature change, a move within the file, a rename-and-restore. The referrer in pkg/a.go is live and would be reported if the check looked only at what the removed text deleted, so the silence proves the kept-set is consulted. Replaces the two cases that caught nothing: referenced-nowhere (no referrer enrolled, so nothing could fire) and no-deletion (no removed text, so the check never ran)

name: go-dangling-lists-every-referrer-asks
desc: a deleted def with TWO live cross-file referrers: the ask must name both. Pins the referrer list itself, not just the fact that an ask happened — expect_symbols carries the referrer paths, so truncating the list (the maxDanglingReferrers cap firing early) fails this fixture. The cap is what keeps a hostile or generated repo from padding a permission prompt with hundreds of paths, and it sat unpinned through two rounds of scoring because every other fixture asserts only the deleted symbol's name
